about: One entry per release that needs more than a redeploy. `coderhelm-selfhost update` prints every entry between the installed and the target version, and stops at an entry with breaking: true until it is run again with --yes (after doing what the entry says). An entry with breaking: true should also have "action": what to do, in one sentence; the installer and the dashboard show it. Releases with no entry are plain redeploys: tables and buckets keep their data, items only gain fields.

releases.notes: First self-host release: one config file, the single-origin web stack, Bedrock as a model provider, setup checks with fixes (doctor, Settings then Setup) and update readiness. The v0.2.x to v0.6.0 tags are from before self-hosting and have no releases.

Self-hosted installs no longer offer Sign in with Google: the update removes the Google identity provider (integrations.googleSignIn is ignored). Also: hybrid installs can link a Jira site through CoderHelm, and Deliveries and Setup show email by kind and the sender's state.
releases.action: If people signed in to this install with Google, tell them to sign in with Forgot password on the same email after the update; they keep their account. Then run the update again with --yes.
